messages:
kevin: Quick heads-up — I sketched a migration proposal for ingest/console storage. Goal: move 'consumption_window' from tenant scope to being scoped by route_profile + region_shard so we can enforce per-route quotas and region failover independently.
ashwin: Can you paste the proposal? curious about backfill plan / perf impact.
kevin: pasted below. TL;DR: add route_profile_id (uuid) and region_shard (string) to compact_events table, compute new shard via mapping table, dual-write for 2w, then backfill in batches keyed by tenant->route; small shadow index first.
maria: Why route_profile rather than route_id? will that explode cardinality on console queries?
kevin: route_profile normalizes many route variants (same logical route across tenants). route_id is too fine-grained and would break aggregation. route_profile keeps cardinality manageable.
sara: What about dashboards that currently roll-up by tenant+window? we'll need UI change to let users pick 'route profile' or 'all routes'.
kevin: yep — console changes planned: default UX stays tenant-level; an advanced filter adds route_profile. We'll also add a migration flag so old dashboards keep working for 1mo.
ashwin: Backfill strategy? need to avoid causing bloat on hot partitions.
kevin: Backfill plan:
1) create nullable columns: route_profile_id, region_shard
2) deploy dual-write at ingest for new arrivals (writes both legacy and new fields)
3) add small partial index on (route_profile_id, consumption_window) marked as CONCURRENTLY
4) run ranged backfill per tenant using time-bucketed jobs, rate-limited by CPU and IOPS
5) once coverage hits 100% and dashboards validated, flip read path to prefer new columns
kevin: snippet of the dual-write pseudo:
```
INSERT INTO compact_events (...) VALUES (...)
ON CONFLICT (...) DO UPDATE SET route_profile_id = EXCLUDED.route_profile_id,
                                 region_shard = EXCLUDED.region_shard;
```
maria: I worry about index bloat with region_shard. How many shards do we expect per region?
kevin: expected 4-8 per region for now. We can make region_shard low-cardinality (e.g., hot/cold/priority/legacy) if needed and keep it nullable.
sara: How will this affect TTL/retention and compaction jobs?
kevin: retention unchanged. Compaction will get a minor rewrite to merge based on route_profile first. We added a toggle to keep old compactor behaviour while we validate metrics.
ops-bot: deploy plan note: create feature-flag 'route_profile_ingest_v1' before dual-write, enable in canary, monitor 5xx and p99 latency for 30m.
ashwin: Monitoring: we should add an alert for growth in write amplification (delta bytes/writes) and a dashboard to compare query latencies against baseline.
kevin: agreed — I added a dashboard draft in the proposal doc (link: https://redwood.internal/proposals/consumption-shard-sweep). It includes: write amplification, backfill progress, index size, query p95/p99.
maria: One more thing — analytics jobs that drive billing rely on tenant-aggregation. We must ensure billing reads from legacy fields until cutover.
kevin: yes billing team consulted. Billing will read from legacy columns until we flip a cutover flag; we'll dual-aggregate during transition.
sara: Any plan for rollback if we hit an unforeseen spike during backfill?
kevin: rollback steps:
- pause backfill workers
- revert compactor toggle
- flip feature-flag off to stop dual-writes
- revert read-path to legacy columns (quick DB view swap)
maria: Sounds reasonable. Can you add an FAQ about why we chose route_profile vs route_id, and expected storage delta per 1B events?
kevin: will do. Estimate: ~7-12% storage overhead during backfill peak due to dual writes, then ~3% steady-state for new columns and indexes.
ashwin: approve to move to RFC stage. please add runbook steps for on-call and a preflight checklist.
kevin: filed RFC and preflight checklist. tagging @sara @maria for review. :rocket:
deploy-bot: RFC created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026-03-consumption-window-sharding — reviewers: sara, maria, ashwin.
